help.open: Open the guide for this tab
help.intro: The app reads the same thing you see on screen during a battle and remembers it for you. Nothing needs to be configured in the game.
help.start.title: Getting started
help.start.text:
Launch the game and the app — the order does not matter.
Open Settings and enter your in-game nickname. This is the only required step: without it the app cannot tell your team from the enemy.
The clan tag is not needed. If you are «[CLAN] Username» in game, just write «Username».
help.status.title: How to tell it is working
help.status.text:
There is a dot and a label in the top right corner.
Green «In battle» — a battle is running and the table is filling up.
Yellow «In hangar» — the game is running but you are not in a battle.
Red «Game not running» — the app does not see the game. Check that War Thunder is actually running; if it has just started, give it half a minute.
help.who.title: Why not every player is listed
help.who.text:
The game does not expose a full roster — there is simply no way to get one.
A player appears in the table only after they kill someone, damage someone, or die. A couple of minutes into a battle that is usually most of the team, but never all of it and never instantly.
This is a limitation of the game, not a gap in the app.
help.table.title: What the battle columns mean
help.table.text:
K, D, A — kills, losses and assists. An assist is when you damaged an enemy and someone else finished them off; the game does not report this, the app works it out itself.
★ — awards earned this battle. Hover to see the list.
Status — «in battle», «destroyed · picking» (lost the vehicle but still playing), «left», «not deployed».
help.icons.title: Icons and colours
help.icons.text:
▮ ground vehicle, ◬ anti-air, ✈ plane, ⊹ helicopter.
The vehicle column shows one chip per sortie, left to right. The last one is the current vehicle. A struck-through chip means the vehicle was lost; ×N next to it is the frags scored in it.
Your own row is highlighted in blue.
A gold outline marks whoever killed you last — the target for «Eye for an Eye». It disappears on its own once the award is out of reach.
help.stats.title: Statistics
help.stats.text:
The four tiles at the top count battles: since the app was launched, today, this week and this month. Each resets separately, and resetting deletes nothing — the count simply starts over.
Below are the charts: which hours you play and when you win more often, win and loss streaks, KDA and win rate by day, and a six-month activity calendar.
Hover over any bar or square for a tooltip with the exact numbers.
help.history.title: Battle history and search
help.history.text:
The History tab holds every recorded battle. Click a row to see the full roster.
Search covers both nicknames and vehicle names — type «T-80» or an enemy nickname.
Filters stack: for example «this month» + «win» + «in the IS-2». The numbers above the list are the wins and KDA of what was found, not of the whole database.
help.size.title: Interface size
help.size.text:
If the text is too small, open Settings and increase the interface size. There are five steps up to maximum.
The whole window scales, charts and tables included — nothing falls out of place.
help.window.title: Keeping the window over the game
help.window.text:
The «Keep window on top» option works when the game runs in borderless windowed mode.
In exclusive fullscreen Windows will not show any program over the game — that is a limitation of the operating system. Switch the game to borderless windowed if you need the window on top.
help.data.title: Where the data lives
help.data.text:
The whole history is kept in a single file on your computer. The «Show database file» button in Settings opens the folder containing it.
To make a copy, simply copy that file somewhere else.
Before any destructive operation the app makes a backup next to the file, and the action requires typing a confirmation word — a stray click costs nothing.
help.problems.title: If something goes wrong
help.problems.text:
The table is empty during a battle — check that your nickname is entered in Settings.
Allies and enemies are swapped — usually the nickname is misspelled or written with the clan tag.
An «unrecognised kill-feed lines» block appeared in Settings — the app met a phrasing it does not know. Copy those lines and send them to the author; that is how the list grows.
The table clears when a new battle starts, not when you die or return to the hangar.
about.what: Sightline reads the War Thunder kill feed, shows who is fighting in what vehicle right now, and builds up a history of battles and players.
about.disclaimer: Not affiliated with or endorsed by Gaijin Entertainment. War Thunder is a trademark of Gaijin Entertainment; the name is used here only to state compatibility.
about.fair: Only the official local interface the game opens itself is used (127.0.0.1:8111). The app neither reads nor modifies game files, and shows nothing you cannot already see on your own screen.
tray.stillRunning: The app keeps running in the tray. To quit for good, right-click the tray icon and choose Quit.
settings.closeToTrayHint: to quit for good, right-click the tray icon
settings.launchWithSystemHint: starts quietly, straight into the tray
settings.showOnGameStart: Show the window when War Thunder starts
settings.hideOnGameExit: Hide the window when the game closes
settings.launchNote: A separate "start with the game" option is not needed: the app notices the game coming up on its own and opens. For that it has to be running in the tray — enable starting with Windows.
help.tray.title: Tray and startup
help.tray.text:
By default the close button does not quit the app but hides it in the tray — the icon next to the clock. To quit for good, right-click that icon and choose Quit.
Settings can start the app with Windows: it launches quietly straight into the tray and opens by itself once you start War Thunder.
There is no separate "start with the game" switch, and there cannot be: to notice the game starting, the app already has to be running. That is exactly why it waits in the tray.
cancel.feedGap: Part of the battle events was lost — this battle will not count towards statistics.
cancel.serverLost: Connection to the server was lost during the battle — it will not count towards statistics.
acc.guest.title: You are using the app without an account
acc.guest.text: The app works fully this way: the battle table, history, statistics and player dossiers. Everything stays on your computer and is sent nowhere.
acc.guest.why1: Cross-checking battle records with other players — this is how real statistics are told apart from fabricated ones.
acc.guest.why2: A public profile and the ability to view other players’ ones.
acc.changePasswordSiteHint: Your password is shared by all projects and is changed on feelyamon.ru — the page opens in your browser.
acc.loginHint: Latin letters, digits and _ - . ; from 3 to 24 characters
acc.warnTitle: What happens to the history you already have
acc.warnText: Battles recorded before registration stay on your computer but will not count towards the shared ranking: their authenticity cannot be confirmed. Everything you play from now on will count.
acc.signOutHint: the app keeps working, your history stays where it is
acc.signOutAllText: Every sign-in will be closed — on other computers and here as well. You can sign back in with the same login and password.
acc.changePasswordHint: Changing the password issues a new recovery code and retires the old one. Every sign-in on other devices will be closed.
acc.offline: No connection to the server. The app works as usual, try again later.
code.title: Recovery code
code.lead: This is the only way to regain access if you forget your password. We collect no email, and the code is shown once and never again — we do not have it, only a hash.
code.confirm: I have saved the code somewhere safe
totp.title: Authenticator code
totp.lead: Two-factor sign-in is enabled for this account. Open your authenticator app (Google Authenticator or compatible) and enter the six digits for Feelyamon.
totp.leadBackup: No phone at hand? Enter one of the backup codes you received when two-factor sign-in was enabled. Each code works once.
totp.useBackup: I don’t have my phone — use a backup code
totp.bad: The code did not match. Make sure your phone sets its time automatically and enter a fresh code.
totp.expired: Time to enter the code has run out. Sign in again with your login and password.
totpSetup.title: Set up two-factor sign-in
totpSetup.lead: Your role requires a second factor: without it you cannot sign in to any project. This takes a minute.
totpSetup.step1: Install an authenticator app on your phone — Google Authenticator or any compatible one.
totpSetup.step2: Scan the QR code below. No camera? Enter the secret manually.
totpSetup.step3: Enter the six digits the app shows.
backup.title: Backup codes
backup.lead: If you lose your phone, you can sign in with one of these codes instead of the six digits. Each works once. The codes are shown only now — save them.
backup.confirm: I have saved the backup codes

acc.gameNickOptional: you can leave it empty and fill it in later in settings
update.title: The app is out of date
update.text: The server refused to work with this build. Update the app — with an old version your statistics would go nowhere, and you would never find out.

battle.unknownHint: Teams are worked out from the kill feed: until someone kills or damages someone, there is nothing to split. From there the links spread along the chain — the moment anyone here meets your team, that whole half moves to Allies or Enemies at once.

acc.proof: Proving you are not a bot… {n}k
player.friend: A friend. Which side they are on is unknown — put them in your squad if you are playing together
friends.title: Friends
friends.needAccount: Friends come with an account: the list lives on the server, otherwise there would be nothing to share it through. See the Account tab.
friends.addSlot: Invite a friend to the squad
friends.clickToRemove: Click to take out of the squad
friends.squadNote: The squad here is your own list, not the in-game one: the game does not expose its roster and the app cannot invite anyone into it. What it does give you: everyone you put here counts as your side, so teams in battle are worked out at once instead of waiting for the first kills.
friends.noGameNick: has not stated a game nick — cannot be recognised in battle
acc.avatarHint: PNG or JPEG, up to one megabyte. The server crops it to a square and scales it to 128 pixels; the original is not kept. The avatar is shown in your profile, so everyone can see it.
delBattle.title: Delete this battle?
delBattle.text: The battle will disappear from history and from the charts. It cannot be brought back — the game will not hand out that kill feed again.
delBattle.confirmedText: Another participant submitted a record of this battle and it matched yours. Such a battle is evidence for your statistics, so delete it only deliberately. Accumulated totals (battles played, wins) do not change: recomputing them from a shortened history would let anyone paint their own statistics by deleting bad battles.
delBattle.agree: I understand I am deleting a confirmed battle
trust.confirmed:
Battle confirmed: another participant submitted a matching record.
Battles like this count towards public statistics and rankings.
trust.disputed:
Discrepancy: someone else's record of this battle did not match yours.
It does not count towards public statistics while an administrator reviews it.
In your own history it stays as it is.
trust.guest:
Not verified — recorded while signed out.
This battle is stored only on this computer: it is not sent to the server and does not count towards your account statistics, neither now nor after you sign in.
report.title: Report a problem
report.lead: Describe what went wrong and what you were doing before that. The more precise the steps, the better the chance it gets fixed rather than forgotten.
report.placeholder: What happened, what you were doing, what you expected to see
report.tooShort: Describe the problem in at least a couple of sentences — one word cannot be fixed
card.reportHint: The report goes to an administrator together with your login — there are no anonymous reports, they cannot be reviewed otherwise. Describe what actually happened: "played badly" cannot be acted on.
card.reportPlaceholder: chat abuse, deliberate teamkill, suspected cheating — with details
card.reportSent: Report sent. An administrator will review it.
player.isUser: Uses Sightline — there will be someone to confirm this battle

report.stepsPlaceholder: step by step — if you know
report.attachToggle: Attach details about the app — they make it far easier to sort out
report.needTag: Choose what the report is about.
acc.statsVerified: All recorded battles are counted. A battle confirmed by other players counts as verified — those will be shown separately.
acc.privacyHint: Hides your statistics from others. The nickname underline in battle stays: it says a person uses the app, not what their numbers are.
update.nothingToSay: See the site for what changed.
forced.title: Set a new password
forced.lead: An administrator declared your previous password invalid. You set the new one yourself — nobody else will know it. You will need the recovery code issued when you registered.
forced.codeHint: sixteen characters; dashes and case do not matter
forced.done: Password set. Save the new recovery code — the previous one no longer works.
profile.title: Player profile
profile.searchHint: in-game nickname or login, three characters or more
profile.confirmedHint: A battle counts as confirmed when its record matches another user’s. Few confirmed battles is not a reproach: most often there simply was no second user around.
notify.title: Notifications
notify.avatarRemoved: Your avatar was removed from your profile for a violation.
notify.avatarBanned: Your avatar was removed from your profile for a violation. You can no longer set an avatar.
notify.friendRequest: {login} wants to add you as a friend.
notify.passwordReset: An administrator declared your password invalid. Set a new one.
report.queued: No connection to the server. The report is saved and will be sent as soon as the connection is back.
report.disputedHint: Tick the battles you disagree with. Your own record of each — time, roster and score — is attached automatically. Only your own battles carrying a discrepancy mark can be attached.
report.disputedNone: No disputed battles. The mark appears when someone else’s record of a battle disagrees with yours — you have none.
acc.privacyAdminOnly: Available to administrators only for now.
guest.title: You are not signed in
guest.text: Battles recorded while signed out are not verified: they stay on this computer only and count towards neither account statistics nor rankings. Signing in later will not upload them either — only battles played after you sign in are counted.
guest.local: Battle breakdown, history and charts work without an account.
